cs.t: My desktop is still a 2017 iMac Pro and I’m holding out for a workstation-class machine with similarly excellent speakers & display, pitched at the same target market but contemporary spec main board.  The standard iMac is not up to this level, and hard pass on the M5 Ultra Studio + Studio Display combo, I like the integrated form factor too much.  In the meantime I work mostly on MBP. Fortunately, I am patient.

They seem to want those who would’ve bought a high spec iMac (or briefly, an iMac Pro) to instead buy a midrange-or-above Mini or a Studio instead. With the M-series, the iMac returned to its roots as the “family computer” or “grandma email box” kind of machine. It’s too bad. A high end iMac still holds a lot of appeal, especially for those seeking clean desk setups. I’m using an MBP hooked up to dual monitors through a dock right now and it’s fine, but I do miss how clean my desk was back when it was a VESA mounted iMac Pro and companion monitor.

I thought so too when I bought a beefy iMac Pro in 2017. But then guess what, new CPU architecture and 10 years down the line it's not supported anymore. Yes I can stay on whatever OS was last supported, but the tools also start ditching support slowly. For example, Rust no longer has tier 1 support for x86_64-apple-darwin so it's a matter of time when things will start breaking. I am quite sure Apple will think of a reason to deprecate my M1 Macbook Pro (which works great BTW!) in a couple of years, at which point I'm switching back to Linux and will not be coming back. I'm tired of accumulating perfectly good hardware in my house which is nerfed by lack of software updates.
cs.th: Apple introduces M6 and M5 Ultra for a big leap in performance and AI compute

cs.t: I’m still using a 2017 iMac Pro as a desktop sidecar for almost anything that doesn’t require a current-generation CPU/GPU or colossal memory bandwidth. The speakers are great, so is the 5k Retina display.

Actually you are correct. I've been following the HN threads about Tahoe and even watched a few YouTube videos and could only facepalm. But then again I'll get rid of the iMac Pro this year. I'll have technicians butcher it and salvage whatever they can from it -- I suspect only the SSD will survive -- and will them hollow it out and put a R1811 board inside it so I can use it as a proper standalone 5K screen. I don't care about Macs anymore, they limit me too much and I can't maintain multiple Linux machines just when I figure I would want to do something that Macs can't do (like experiment with bcachefs or ZFS pools and volumes and snapshots for my continually evolving backup setup).
cs.th: More Mac malware from Google search

cs.t: As many people mentioned my work computer is a mac chosen by the employer. My major issues with iMac Pro, which by the way is nice piece of machine overall, rises when I'm using non-commercialized applications, open source mainly, github projects, conda forge etc. My personal laptop is refurbished dell latitude 7470 which I bought for less than 300$ at 2019 despite the fact I replaced many parts does the job and I like the sturdiness.
cs.th: Ask HN: What brand of laptop do you use?

cs.t: I agree with what you are saying up until you say nothing is wrong with the fan coming on at a 15% cpu load. regardless of what is really happening to take that 15% load, if the fan comes on that strong, it is not a proper thermal design. As a contrast, I have an 8 core iMac Pro. It can run full throttle and I rarely if ever hear the fan and it is  much  quieter than my 2018 6 core macbook pro. Of course a 27" home chassis has much more room to dissapate heat, but that is the point. Shoving oversized processors with multiple cores that generate lots of heat is at odds with Jony Ive's add more thinness campaign. I am now in a position where I use my macbook for dev and more intensive uses and its so damn annoying that Im seriously considering getting rid of it. I was at a client site this week, and my laptop was constantly the but of the joke, and disruptive to 5 other people working in a conference room. Sorry, but that just sucks...

We are 100% remote with an optional co-working space that is available if you ever want to work at an “office” environment. Project is managed mostly through airtable with quarterly goals with weekly’s and daily’s (not standup) to check on progress. Then we have a company/team wide call every tues for the weekly brief. All the above enabled me to have the best environment by then investing in my home office. A space that has a good desk (multitable sit/stand), chair (aeron), and good lighting, not to mention a beautiful machine (iMac Pro). The issues that followed were more of the focus issues when doing work at home, so I got a pomodoro clock which then made everything seamless.
cs.th: Ask HN: What company environment has enabled your best work?

cs.t: I would advise folks to hold off on this. I've a base configuration iMac Pro. There is an issue with either the video card, T2 chip or some combination of the 2.(or maybe something entirely different) There is a kernel panic issue that has yet to be solved, even though there is a very long thread going on the apple support community. Ive been contacted by apple engineers based on my participation in the thread, so I believe they are on the verge of officially acknowledging a problem here. So far those affected have done everything from re-imaging, replacing and returning their iMac Pros and nothing has fixed this issue. I want to upgrade my macbook pro, but until they fix this, Im not buying any more macs...
cs.th: MacBook Pro with faster performance and new features for pros

cs.t: > they said they were waiting for a higher memory variant M6 That's not what they said. I gathered they were waiting for an iMac refresh, with the hopes that iMac Pro would get an upgrade. Hence the "would be nice to have some kind of a pro model" > most people buying high-RAM machines want to bring their own monitor The 27" iMac Pro 5K is holding its value pretty well on second-hand markets, despite its age. The Mac Studio replaced the Mac Pro, not the iMac Pro.

The thing that makes older iMacs "disposable" is that the required cooling vents end up [mostly] blocked, within just a few years – then they thermally throttle, until death. If you open them up and keep them clean, they can have uses  forever : ---- My 27" iMac (2009) still sits faithfully alongside my main 48" setup (because I own the copy of CS4 installed upon it – FU Adobe!). It mostly plays background shows (while I work on main computer, adjacent). My 24" iMac (2006) still sits faithfully on my tax desk, for its annual usage/filing. It also still plays Warcraft 3: Frozen Throne (quite well!). ---- >I suggest spending a bit more and getting a mac mini and a ... display, instead This is fantastic advice; my past two Apple's have been Mini's. My three main machines all connect to the same massive 48" display (that is about to outlast its first retired Mini). The only new iMac I would ever again consider purchasing would be something on-par with the iMac Pro (2017) – but in 2026+ any iMac would need a 32"+ display (minimum) to be "usable" IMHO.
